A1.justification: Both PDFs clearly describe ClinRaGen, and their main text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 ends at the references despite citing Appendices A–E; v2 includes Appendices A.1–A.8. Earlier supplemental details and results therefore cannot be fully matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original disease-diagnosis experiments, component ablations, GPT-4 and human rationale evaluations, and clinical case studies on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV.

after.justification: v2 retains original diagnostic and rationale evaluations and reports additional comparator, model-configuration, teacher-selection and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: Knowledge acquisition expands from PubMed abstracts to documents from PubMed and Wikipedia. The broad encoder–attention–SLM architecture, three distillation objectives and freezing schedule remain. Vocabulary filtering and prefix integration receive more explicit descriptions, without clearly establishing a replacement of the underlying attention procedure.

E1.justification: The clinical coverage remains the same: 28,456 MIMIC-III records, 28,900 MIMIC-IV records and 25 disease phenotypes using notes and laboratory time series. Supporting knowledge coverage expands to Wikipedia disease documents alongside PubMed material; no new clinical benchmark or diagnostic task is introduced.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds zero-shot LLaMA and ChatGPT diagnostic comparisons and a Clinical CoT variant with a time-series encoder, retaining the note-only variant. These substantially expand the comparison controls. The rationale-generation comparator set—Mistral, LLaMA2 and LLaMA3—remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds the 793M ClinRaGen configuration and a student/teacher evaluation grid involving Flan-T5, OPT, QWEN and ChatGPT versus DeepSeek. Table 1 changes the reported LLaMA inputs from notes alone to notes plus labs. Human evaluators are described as 15 professional postgraduates instead of 15 qualified clinicians; this is a reported setting revision, without establishing that evaluation was rerun. Dataset splits and evaluation sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original three component ablations remain, renamed from ClinRaGen-I/II/III to w/o LAB&KNOW, KNOW and REASONING. New Table 6 tests dependence on student architecture, size and teacher, including paired removal of labs and knowledge. Table 3 adds computational-cost analysis. The two clinical cases are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: v2 first states five-run averaging and t-testing at p < 0.05; v1 provides neither disclosure. Table 1 adds parenthetical quantities, although their statistical meaning and scale are unspecified. v2 also reports intra-class and inter-class agreement of 0.637 and 0.608. These additions do not establish an increase from a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise numerical results: the 87M ClinRaGen micro F1 entries change from 0.6413/0.6991 to 0.6410/0.6989 on MIMIC-III/IV. v2 adds larger-model, comparator, timing and student/teacher results, and supplies previously unavailable BLEU/BERTScore results. These are revised or newly reported outcomes, not demonstrated same-setting gains. New Figure 5 also conflicts with Table 1: ClinRaGen* is plotted above 0.715 on MIMIC-IV, whereas the table reports 0.7127.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 5 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the knowledge-filtered vocabulary, including its relationship to the standard vocabulary. The original generation and distillation objectives otherwise retain their substance. Equation 6 mainly expands the previously described cross-attention operation; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain knowledge-augmented attention and sequential multimodal rationale distillation. However, v2's abstract and contribution list assert state-of-the-art rationale-generation performance, strengthening v1's emphasis on rationales comparable to LLMs. Shared-space encoding receives more explicit emphasis.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning inherited teacher biases, external-knowledge quality and coverage, and applicability beyond the evaluated EHR setting. Appendices A.7–A.8 discuss student and teacher selection. Retained cases are reinterpreted as mitigating teacher bias, and weak zero-shot performance is newly treated as evidence ruling out leakage—a conclusion those results do not establish.

D1.justification: v2 supplies previously unavailable anomaly templates, rationale prompts, software versions, optimizer settings, learning rate, warm-up, GPU hardware and time-series padding/patch details. It adds a code-access link, dataset-access instructions and nearest-value imputation documentation. These are disclosures rather than established setting changes. Conversely, v1's explicit PatchTST identification and note-cleaning description disappear.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion and citations for MedAdapter, rationale-guided medical RAG and knowledge-graph community retrieval, sharpening its discussion of retrieval limitations. Several earlier references, including PatchTST and prefix-tuning work, disappear. The broader positioning around efficient clinical rationale distillation and external knowledge remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and substantial methodological prose are rewritten. Experimental subsections are consolidated, distillation stages receive explicit phase headings, and evaluation-criterion definitions move to Appendix A.5. Limitations, ethics and supplemental discussions are added. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond scientific additions alone.

P2.justification: v2 adds a motivation diagram and parameter/performance plots, substantially redraws the architecture diagram, and expands Table 1 with grouped comparisons, a size column and parenthetical statistics. Table 2 is reorganized, and Tables 3–6 supply additional displays. Earlier rationale radar charts and case examples are retained with formatting, labeling and placement changes.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the work more reproducible and assessable by supplying omitted prompt/training documentation, adding a multimodal Clinical CoT control and student/teacher checks, and reporting repeated runs and evaluator agreement. The net gain is limited by unexplained statistical quantities, inconsistencies between Figure 5 and Table 1, and unsupported strengthening of leakage and rationale-superiority claims. These problems temper the benefits of the substantially expanded documentation and evaluation.
